'''Hoyahoya''' (Matakia)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.3 - Hoyahoya-Matakaia |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/hoya1235 |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref> is an [[Anim languages|Anim language]] spoken in the village of Matakaia ({{coord|-7.845775|143.246807|type:city_region:PG|name=Gagoro - Matakaia}}) of [[Bamu Rural LLG]] in [[Western Province, Papua New Guinea]].<ref name="Ethnologue22-PNG">{{cite web |date=2019 |editor1-last=Eberhard |editor1-first=David M. |editor2-last=Simons |editor2-first=Gary F. |editor3-last=Fennig |editor3-first=Charles D. |title=Papua New Guinea languages |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/country/PG/languages |work=[[Ethnologue]]: Languages of the World |publisher=[[SIL International]] |edition=22nd |location=Dallas}}</ref><ref name="UN-PNG">{{cite web |author=United Nations in Papua New Guinea |date=2018 |title=Papua New Guinea Village Coordinates Lookup |url=https://data.humdata.org/dataset/village-coordinates-lookup |work=Humanitarian Data Exchange |version=1.31.9}}</ref> It shares its name with the closely related [[Hoia Hoia language]]. It is documented solely in an unpublished wordlist by Carr (1991).<ref>Carr, Philip J. 1991 ''Foyafoya (Bibisa, W.P. at Kamusi), Hoyahoya (Matakaia, W.P. at Gagoro), Hoyahoya/Hoiahoia (Ukusi-Koperami, W.P. two young men visiting Torobina)''. Manuscript.</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book |title=The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide |date=2018 |publisher=De Gruyter Mouton |isbn=978-3-11-028642-7 |editor-last=Palmer |editor-first=Bill |series=The world of linguistics |location=Berlin ; Boston}}</ref>
